quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Switch between high beam and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used on high beam.
questions.explanation: Using your high beam headlight during the day helps other drivers see you. Use high beam any time you are not riding behind or toward other vehicles.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator:
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show what they plan to do. A bent left arm pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A single-file formation is best when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. While staggered formation is good for staying together, single-file gives each rider the most safety in curves.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you will want to adjust the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: A larger cushion of space may not be necessary if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are not perfect. Add more space if the pavement is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Each traffic lane gives the motorcyclist how many paths of travel?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: the left side, center, and right side of the lane.

questions.question: If braking in a curve:

options.text: It will be the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: When braking while turning, some of your tire's traction is used to make the turn. This means less traction is available for stopping.

questions.question: When you are being passed by a vehicle on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding to the side nearest the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding to the far side may make the other driver merge back too soon. Stay centered.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Close to the back of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This way they do not have to chase the group, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see better and be seen. It should keep you out of blind spots and away from hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route if needed.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake lever.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the handlebars first, then stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the handlebars first, then stop.
questions.explanation: Straighten and square the handlebars before stopping quickly. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors help others see you while riding. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: When turning left, which handgrip should you press?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward to make the motorcycle lean in that direction.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
The best position depends on the riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on the riding conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best. Choose a position based on your riding conditions. This helps you keep safe distance and stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ times more likely to suffer a critical head injury.
questions.correctAnswerText: Five
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Wear hearing protection all the time to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks out horns and sirens.
Do not wear hearing protection if you have a full-face helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection all the time to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing and still let you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When turning, how should you look where you want to go?

options.text: Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: As an operator, which of the following should you NOT tell a passenger to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as close forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the handholds, your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: If you need to brake while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the turn to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle leans than when it is upright. Try to straighten up before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Gender, physical condition, and food intake may also have an effect.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Move around your lane as needed to see better, be seen, and maintain safe space.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Learns and remembers the braking force used by the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your braking system.
